q: A paramedic course is at least about:
why: Paramedic ALS training is at least about 1,000 hours.

q: Screenings and early blood-pressure care are examples of:
why: Secondary prevention catches problems early, such as screenings and early BP care.

q: A knowledge-based error is choosing the wrong plan because the problem is:
why: Knowledge-based errors happen on new, incomplete problems — the wrong plan or antidote.

q: The correct order to put on PPE is:
why: On goes clean hands, gown, mask, eyes, then gloves.

q: Stress that shows days to months later with nightmares is:
why: Delayed stress hits days to months later, often with nightmares or flashbacks.

q: At a hazmat scene, you should stage:
why: Hazmat staging is uphill and upwind from the spill.

q: Implied consent applies when the patient is:
choices: alert and refusing after full risks
awake but angry about the bill
signing a living will at home
why: Implied consent covers an unresponsive or badly altered patient in a true emergency.

q: Dependent lividity is a:
why: Lividity is a definitive sign of death, not a presumptive one.

q: Capacity to refuse care requires they can:
why: Capacity needs understanding, the downside, reasoning, and a communicated choice.

q: A patient care report should hold:
why: PCR is facts only — not documented means it did not happen.

q: You transfer care only after a verbal handoff plus:
why: Handoff needs a verbal report to equal or higher care and a finished PCR.

q: During an interview you should avoid:
why: Avoid false reassurance, leading questions, jargon, and judgment.

q: The root hepat- means:
why: Hepat- means liver; cardi- is heart; nephr- is kidney.

q: Proximal means closer to the:
why: Proximal is closer to the trunk; distal is farther out.

q: The cervical spine has how many vertebrae?
why: Cervical is 7; then 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 fused sacrum, 4 fused coccyx.

q: Beta-1 receptors mainly make the heart:
why: Beta-1 is one heart: faster and harder beat.

q: The AV node’s main job is to:
choices: pause so the ventricles can fill
why: The AV node pauses so the ventricles have time to fill.

q: A power grip for lifting uses palms up about:
why: Power grip is palms up about 10 inches apart.

q: An urgent move is roughly about:
why: Urgent is about one minute; emergency is seconds and may skip spine.

q: A scoop stretcher is especially useful for a:
why: The scoop splits and is used for hip-fracture moves.

q: In OPQRST, the letter Q asks for:
why: Q is quality — their word for the pain. Do not lead with left-arm talk.

q: A rapid trauma scan should take about:
why: The rapid scan is about 60 seconds.

q: Adult positive-pressure ventilation is considered if the rate is:
why: Think about bagging an adult if faster than 28 or slower than 8.

q: Your SpO2 goal for most patients is about:
why: SpO2 goal is about 94–99 percent.

q: A tourniquet on a limb goes:
why: Tourniquet goes closer to the body (proximal) on an arm or leg.

q: A nasal cannula is typically run at:
why: Cannula flow is about 1–6 LPM.

q: CPAP for lung fluid needs the patient alert, sitting, and systolic at least:
why: CPAP needs alert, sitting, fluid picture, and SBP at least 90.

q: No trauma story and a medical collapse. Open the airway with:
why: Medical with no spine worry uses head-tilt chin-lift.

q: A mild choking adult who still coughs and moves air gets:
why: Mild choke: still moving air — hands off and encourage cough.

q: The pin-index system means an oxygen regulator fits:
why: Pin-index: oxygen regulator only on an oxygen tank.

q: Nitroglycerin may be repeated every 5 minutes up to:
why: Nitro is 0.4 mg SL, every 5 minutes, max three doses.

q: Hold nitroglycerin if they took a -fil sexual med within:
why: Hold nitro after Viagra/Cialis/Levitra-type (-fil) drugs in the last 24 hours.

q: Adult epinephrine for anaphylaxis is:
why: Adult epi auto-injector is 0.3 mg IM in the lateral thigh.

q: Anaphylaxis is an allergic reaction involving:
why: Anaphylaxis means allergic findings in two or more systems.

q: Flushed warm skin with low blood pressure suggests:
why: Flushed warm skin with low pressure means the vessels are dilated (sepsis or anaphylaxis).

q: In tension pneumothorax, breath sounds are usually:
why: Tension has absent sounds on one side; equal clear points to tamponade.

q: Cardiogenic shock after a big MI often adds:
why: Cardiogenic: weak pump — shock plus chest pain and lung crackles.

q: Two rescuers doing child CPR use a ratio of:
why: Two-rescuer child or infant CPR is 15:2; single rescuer stays 30:2.

q: Infant compression depth is about:
why: Infant depth is about one-third of the chest, roughly 1.5 inches.

q: Adult AED pads go on the:
choices: upper left and lower right chest
both sides of the neck only
center back and left hip only
upper right and lower left chest
why: Adult pads: upper right chest and lower left chest.

q: On a suspected epiglottitis child you should:
why: Epiglottitis: leave the throat alone — no OPA, no deep suction; keep calm and upright.

q: Emphysema is often pictured as a:
choices: sudden tearing pain to the back
why: Emphysema (pink puffer): lost elasticity, barrel chest, pursed-lip breathing.

q: Pink frothy sputum points strongly to:
why: Pink frothy sputum is the classic pulmonary-edema / CHF picture.

q: Left-sided heart failure backs blood into the:
why: Failing left ventricle backs blood into the lungs (crackles, dyspnea).

q: Unstable angina is best described as a:
choices: changing pattern that may hit at rest
pain that always eases with rest
pain that never radiates at all
pain that only lasts under a minute
why: Unstable angina is a changing pattern — less work, at rest, longer, or more nitro.

q: Right-sided heart failure often shows:
why: Right failure backs into the body: JVD and dependent edema.

q: Clot-buster drugs for stroke are often only given within about:
why: Clot-busters are often only inside about 3 hours from onset — get last known well exact.

q: About what share of strokes are hemorrhagic?
why: About 13% are hemorrhagic; about 87% are ischemic.

q: The spleen sits in the left upper quadrant and removes:
why: Spleen is LUQ and removes old red cells; kidneys filter waste.

q: Pancreas pain is mid-upper and can shoot to the:
why: Pancreas is mid-upper and can refer to the back.
